A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DF-MCQ study. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendix A are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original WPU experiments using Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, probing-question evaluations, sensitivity analyses and per-subset results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds results for an SFT attack and continual unlearning of ten individuals in Tables 4 and 5.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same MCQ construction, KL-based distribution-flattening loss, original-model retain loss and balanced minibatches. The additional experiments apply DF-MCQ without introducing a new algorithmic component or objective.

E1.justification: WPU person-centric coverage remains unchanged, but v2 adds scenarios testing whether forgetting persists after an SFT attack and during continual target addition. The ten-person experiment reuses the existing individuals rather than introducing a new dataset or domain.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same original-model, NPO and WHP+ comparators. Newly discussed FLAT and RKLD are not evaluated. The SFT attack is an additional condition applied to DF-MCQ, not a competing unlearning method.

E3.justification: v2 adds post-unlearning fine-tuning on questions about other individuals and a continual ten-person protocol compared with separate two-person unlearning. Existing question counts, splits, metrics, model sizes and the stated three-epoch training procedure remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 7.1 adds focused checks of recoverability after an SFT attack and preservation of forgetting during continual unlearning, reported in new Tables 4 and 5. Existing case studies, alternative distractor splits, learning-rate and obfuscation-sample sensitivity analyses, and Appendix A breakdowns are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions describe averaging standard results across five WPU subsets. Neither adds seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Predictive entropy remains a task metric, not a new statistical uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All matched numerical entries in the existing main-text and appendix tables are unchanged. New v2 Table 4 reports forget/hard-retain scores of 10.70/61.33 after SFT, versus 10.70/60.53 before attack. Table 5 adds continual-ten results of 11.70/58.77 and 91.81% refusal. These are results under added conditions, not revisions to the original experiments.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, entropy criteria and loss equations in Equations 1-8 are unchanged. The new statement about handling any number of targets is an informal extrapolation, without an added theorem, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: distinguishing obfuscation from unlearning, introducing probing evaluations, and using DF-MCQ to obtain refusal and near-random-choice uncertainty. The added experiments do not revise these headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the SFT results as showing persistent refusal and states that continual target additions need not affect previously unlearned targets, extrapolating applicability to any number of targets. These interpretations are new; the existing mechanism discussion and limitations paragraph remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The first-page code pointer changes from the unlearning-hallu repository's mcq branch to the unlearning-dfmcq repository. Existing data-generation, LoRA, hardware and training-time descriptions are retained; detailed SFT-attack and continual-training hyperparameters are not supplied.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds FLAT, RKLD and Hu et al. (2025). It explicitly distinguishes this paper's direct probing from Hu et al.'s fine-tuning-based recovery approach. This is a localized expansion of related work and positioning within the existing taxonomy.

P1.justification: The revision expands the related-work paragraph and adds two labeled discussions in Section 7.1. The section sequence, terminology and most prose remain unchanged, with no extensive rewrite or narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 adds two compact tables, clarifies that Tables 2 and 3 concern open-ended questions, and relocates Figure 5 and Appendix A through page reflow. Existing figures and table structures are retained; appendix Tables 6-8 become Tables 8-10 without changed results.

improvement.justification: Unlike v1, v2 provides checks of persistence after SFT and continual ten-person unlearning, while acknowledging closely related prior work. Tables 4-5 therefore modestly strengthen the empirical coverage. Sparse details for the new protocols, absent statistical uncertainty, and extrapolation from ten targets to arbitrary target counts limit the improvement.
